question: Our platform decides which applicants are admitted to our university programmes, using their transcripts, standardised test scores and socio-economic data. Which AI Act provisions relate to it?
gold_source: Annex III, point 3(a); Article 6(2); Article 6(3), third subparagraph
gold_answer: Annex III, point 3(a) lists AI systems intended to be used to determine access or admission or to assign natural persons to educational and vocational training institutions at all levels, and Article 6(2) makes the AI systems referred to in Annex III high-risk. If the system performs profiling of natural persons, the Article 6(3) exception can never apply (Article 6(3), third subparagraph).

question: Our tool does not decide admissions. It only prepares a short summary of each application for the admission committee, which then assesses every applicant itself. Is there an exception under which it is not high-risk, and what are its conditions?
gold_source: Article 6(3), first subparagraph; Article 6(3), second subparagraph, point (d); Article 6(3), third subparagraph
gold_answer: Under Article 6(3), an Annex III system is not considered high-risk where it does not pose a significant risk of harm to the health, safety or fundamental rights of natural persons, including by not materially influencing the outcome of decision making, and one of the conditions in points (a) to (d) is fulfilled. Point (d) covers a system intended to perform a preparatory task to an assessment relevant for the Annex III use cases. The exception never applies if the system performs profiling of natural persons (Article 6(3), third subparagraph).

question: Our app scores students' assessments and then automatically changes the learning path each student follows. Which AI Act provisions relate to it?
gold_answer: Annex III, point 3(b) lists AI systems intended to be used to evaluate learning outcomes, including when those outcomes are used to steer the learning process of natural persons in educational and vocational training institutions at all levels. Under Article 6(2), the AI systems referred to in Annex III are considered high-risk.

question: Our tool decides whether new students join beginner, intermediate or advanced classes, based on their earlier grades and an aptitude test. Which AI Act provisions relate to it?
gold_answer: Annex III, point 3(c) lists AI systems intended to be used for assessing the appropriate level of education that an individual will receive or will be able to access, in the context of or within educational and vocational training institutions at all levels. Under Article 6(2), the AI systems referred to in Annex III are considered high-risk.

question: During online exams, our platform checks students' code and text for plagiarism and watches their webcam feed to flag cheating in real time. Which AI Act provisions relate to it?
gold_answer: Annex III, point 3(d) lists AI systems intended to be used for monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour of students during tests in the context of or within educational and vocational training institutions at all levels. Under Article 6(2), the AI systems referred to in Annex III are considered high-risk.

question: We want to detect stress and possible cheating in online exams by analysing students' emotions from their webcam video and voice. Which AI Act provisions relate to this?
gold_source: Article 5(1), first subparagraph, point (f); Annex III, point 3(d)
gold_answer: Article 5(1)(f) prohibits placing on the market, putting into service for this specific purpose, or using AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions, except where the use of the AI system is intended to be put in place or into the market for medical or safety reasons. Monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour of students during tests is an Annex III use case (point 3(d)), but being listed in Annex III does not lift the prohibition on inferring emotions.

question: From when do the high-risk rules apply to an AI system that decides student admissions?
gold_source: Article 113, third paragraph, point (c)(i); Annex III, point 3(a)
gold_answer: Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (with the exception of Article 6(5)) apply from 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III, which includes admission systems under Annex III, point 3(a) (Article 113, third paragraph, point (c)(i), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744). The general application date of 2 August 2026 does not apply to these rules.
